summary.title: Audio
summary.one_liner: Learn how to add background music and sound effects to a 2D OpenGL game using the irrKlang audio library.
keywords: manual audio loading vs audio library
takeaways: OpenGL has no built-in audio support, so an audio library such as irrKlang is used instead of manually decoding audio files.
irrKlang is set up by adding its headers, linking irrKlang.lib (64-bit), and copying the DLLs next to the executable; ikpMP3.dll is also needed for MP3 files.
Create an ISoundEngine with createIrrKlangDevice() and call play2D(file, true) to loop background music.
Sound effects are played at collision points (brick hit, solid block, powerup, paddle bounce) to give the player feedback.
irrKlang has a non-commercial free license; commercial use requires its pro version.
summary.summary: This LearnOpenGL chapter explains why audio is missing from the Breakout-style 2D game and introduces irrKlang, a cross-platform sound engine that plays WAV, MP3, OGG and FLAC files. It covers setup (headers, linker settings, DLLs) and the license terms. The chapter then shows how to create a sound engine, loop background music with play2D, and trigger sound effects on collisions such as brick hits, solid blocks, powerups and paddle bounces. The code changes for the sound effects are referenced rather than walked through line by line.
